newsitem.title: USA: Hawke sees Treasury bank plan out before year-end.
newsitem.headline: Hawke sees Treasury bank plan out before year-end.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Undersecretary John Hawke said Thursday he expects the Treasury to issue its bank reform plan before year-end.
He said that the plan would not touch on restructuring bank regulatory agencies.
The Treasury wants to release its plan before Congress reconvenes in early January so that it can be a "focal point," Hawke told a banking litigation seminar.
Legislation passed in September to deal with the undercapitalized thrift deposit insurance fund had a target date of January 1, 1999, for merger of the thrift and bank deposit insurance funds.
"We'd like to hold to that target date," Hawke said. He added that he was "very optimistic" that progress would be made on banking reform in the next Congress.
Hawke said he had no plans to leave his position. Asked whether Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin was staying, Hawke would only say "he's been very committed to his job."
